title: The action of $\operatorname{Aut}(F)$ is transitive
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,F)$ be a Galois category [def-galois-category], $G=\operatorname{Aut}(F)$ and $X$ a connected object [def-galois-connected-object]. Then $G$ acts transitively on $F(X)$.

proof.text: Bundle the finite values of F as the functor F' = ObjectProperty.lift Finite F hCF.finite_obj to FintypeCat. Its composite with FintypeCat.incl is definitionally F. The Stacks exactness and conservativity axioms therefore give preservation of finite limits and colimits and reflection of isomorphisms for F', by reflection along the fully faithful inclusion.

Construct Mathlib's PreGaloisCategory C. Finite limits give the terminal object and pullbacks, and finite colimits give finite coproducts and quotients by finite groups. For the latter, replace a finite group in the hom universe by an isomorphic finite group in Type 0 and transfer colimits along the SingleObj equivalence. The required summand axiom is exactly stacksGalois_mono_complement, from [lem-galois-stacks-mono-complement].

Construct Mathlib's FiberFunctor F'. Preservation of terminal objects, pullbacks, and finite coproducts and reflection of isomorphisms follow from the inherited exactness and conservativity. Clause (2) of [lem-galois-axioms] gives preservation of epimorphisms, since the underlying set maps of epis are surjective. Preservation of finite-group quotients follows from preservation of finite colimits after the same universe reduction as in step 2. Composing F' with FintypeCat.uSwitch supplies a fiber functor in the hom universe, hence a GaloisCategory C instance.

Apply Mathlib CategoryTheory.PreGaloisCategory.FiberFunctor.isPretransitive_of_isConnected to F' and the original connected object X. For x,y choose the resulting natural automorphism g of F'. Whiskering g with FintypeCat.incl gives a natural automorphism of F, whose component at X is the same underlying function, so it sends x to y. This uses Mathlib's already-proved prorepresentability and inverse-limit argument, without the separate Stacks Galois-object existence theorem.

The proof now follows Stacks Lemma 0BN3 (label lemma-tame) in four steps: the directed system of normalized Galois objects, the colimit description of the fibre functor, the compatible inverse system of finite automorphism groups and its induced Aut(F) action, and descent of transitivity along a Galois cover of the given connected object. The nontrivial finite inverse-limit projection fact is isolated as lem-galois-inverse-limit-surjective, with its Stacks 086J source and Mathlib searches. The previous unsupported Mathlib-leaf interpretation and the unused profiniteness dependency were removed.
